summary: Tested the auth/email features: password recovery (backend + UI), creating an operator with a MOCK credentials email, and a code review of the 10-minute idle logout. Backend: 5/5 pytest tests passed. Frontend: 4/4 flows passed (forgot link, forgot page with generic message, reset with mismatched passwords, reset with fake token). Test data was removed (0 residual users operatore.test*/temp.reset*). No real emails were sent: everything went to [EMAIL MOCK].

minor.issue: The JSON response is the same for every email, but the response time is not: for an existing user the endpoint also does DB writes and sends the email inline, so an attacker could tell accounts apart by timing. Possible fix: send the email in a background task.

token_valid_after = now+1s, while iat has 1-second granularity. A login within about 1-2s of the reset gets a token that require_user immediately rejects (401). The UI is not affected in practice because of the 2.5s redirect, but an API client could hit it.

action_items: (Optional) Send the reset email in a background task (asyncio.create_task/BackgroundTasks) to remove the timing difference between existing and non-existing emails
(Optional) Use token_valid_after = int(now.timestamp()) and compare iat with < instead of setting it to +1s, or put the reset timestamp in a separate claim

(Optional) The idle logout is per-tab: a tab left unused logs out (via /auth/logout, which clears the cookie) even if the user is active in another tab. Consider syncing activity through localStorage/BroadcastChannel
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext: the idle logout is implemented correctly (6 activity events, 10-min setTimeout, cleanup on unmount, sonner toast). The only issue is that it is not synced across tabs.
create_user: the credentials email is sent only when accesso_software=true and a password is set. Correct. The password appears only in the email HTML, not in the logs.
server.py is >19000 lines: it should be split into modules.
seed_data_creation: Temporary operator operatore.test.<hex>@example.com created and deleted inside the test (finally block). It also triggered a MOCK reset request for admin@assicura.it; the password was not changed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All email goes to MOCK because SMTP is not configured; check grep '[EMAIL MOCK]' /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. The full reset flow (confirm + session invalidation) was verified by the main agent and was not re-run here so admin's password stays untouched.
